newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 31.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Rugby League chief Neil Whittaker and Super League chief Ian Frykberg met again yesterday in a bid to come to an agreement over the proposed merger of the two competitions for the 1998 season. Whittaker and Frykberg also tried to allay public fears and media speculation that the two groups wouldn't come to a compromise. The fact that former News Ltd chairman and chief executive Ken Cowley attended the meeting is a sign of the seriousness of the situation, as most league observers believe the game will die if the two groups don't form one competition. Page 20.

Kevin Sheedy, the coach Australian Football League club Essendon, has described the growing number of departures from the club as part of a restructuring process. Sheedy, who has been with the team for 18 years, says the club must 'prune the rose bushes' if it wants to go places in the future. So far the 'restructuring' has seen recruiting manager Noel Judkins resign after 16 years and football manager Danny Corcoran move to the Melbourne club. Assistant coach David Wheadon is expected to resign today. age 20.

Australian Rugby Union chief executive John O'Neill has announced plans to stage a Tri-nations test between Australia and the South African Springboks at Perth's Subiaco Oval within two years. This proposal follows the successful showpiece match in Melborne between Australia and New Zealand and is a bid to increase the game's supporter base. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Tim Sheens, coach of the Super League club North Queensland, has criticised the price of tickets to watch a rugby league match, claiming this is the main reason behind dwindling crowd attendances at matches, and not the conflict over the two rival league competitions. Sheens has also warned administrators of the game who watch matches sipping champagne in corporate boxes that they are out of touch with League supporters who sit on the hill eating meat pies. Page 44.

The Sydney United and South Melbourne soccer teams will face the judiciary of Soccer Australia this week charged with bringing the game into disrepute. Soccer Australia chairman David Hill has made many reforms, but the threat to expel Sydney United and Suth Melbourne from the league may be extreme. Page 44.

During the next four weeks the future of the television rights for the Australian Football League after 2001 will be decided. Both the Seven and Nine Networks are seeking to purchase the free-to-air rights of what is considered the premier winter sport inAustralia. Page 44.
THE AGE

Queensland athlete Joanna Stone is in contention for a medal in the women's javelin at the World Championships in Athens after throwing a personal best of 66 metres 44 centimetres. However, Stone says her main aim is to perform well at the 2000 Olympics n Sydney after a disappointing performance at the Atlanta Olympics last year. Page B6.

At the matchplay World Championship of Golf yesterday, played on the River Course at Blackwolf, Ernie Els defeated Steve Elkington in a regional final. Els has advanced to the semi-final where he will play Colin Montgomerie. Page B6.

There will be 33 competitors in this week's skiing aerials World Cup to be held at Mount Buller. American coach Bruce Erickson has described the area as one of the most beautiful in the world. Australian world champion skier Kirsty Marshall who suffered black eye after failing to make a landing on Tuesday, believes it will be much harder for her to win the World Cup this year as her competitors have spent the last 12 months improving their levels of difficulty. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

North Melbourne Australian Football League player David King was suspended by the League's Tribunal last night for two matches for intentionally tripping Carlton player Steve Silvagni in last week's match. Page 80.

The Australian Netball team defeated New Zealand by six goals last night in the Test match played in front of 5000 fans in Hamilton, New Zealand. The match is Australia's 26th consecutive international victory. Page 78
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Apprentice jockey Andrew Gibbons was given a one-month suspension and a A$600 fine at Canterbury yesterday after an incident of interfering which has been described as the worst in Sydney racing in two years. Gibbons was riding Illusive Spy when he made severe move to the fence from the outside barrier, causing the interference. Page 100.

ACT Brumbies rugby union player Owen Finegan will be a reserve player for the Australian Rugby Union side for their Tri-nations match against South Africa on Saturday night at Suncorp Stadium. It is expected Finegan will come into the game at lock as he as been described as too slow to play in the back row. Page 102.

The Manly-Warringah netball team have moved within striking distance of the top four in the Dairy Farmers State Netball League despite the loss of their captain Carissa Tombs through injury. Last night Manly-Warringah defeated Eastwood Ryde 48-43. Page 03.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
